claims.value: The recovered architecture is an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs network: rails carry power and items, production remains modular across protected cores, Rail v.1 starts at 120 items/min, and v.2/v.3 are used only when measured throughput requires 240/480 items/min.

The revised requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers with every Base Core at level 0. Their heavy-machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 against an independent 1,000 capacity per level-0 core. One-core placement is unsafe; every pair is also unsafe because Constructorizer + Facturer = 1,150 and Facturer + Facturer = 1,300. Exceeding 1,000 disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe layout uses three separate level-0 cores: Core C holds only the 500-heat Constructorizer and retains at most 500 heat for all support buildings; Core F1 and Core F2 each hold one 650-heat Facturer and retain at most 350 heat apiece. Any two-heavy-machine co-location is rejected, and each core’s complete measured load must independently remain at or below 1,000.

Before construction, verify the live Update 1 unlock menu and prepare a complete per-core heat ledger including existing load and all support equipment. Then build and recheck Core C, Core F1, and Core F2 sequentially, stopping if any load exceeds 1,000 or Fire Wave protection becomes inactive. Use only confirmed Update 1 equipment: Rails v.1-v.3 are allowed as unlocked and required; Rails v.4-v.5, hidden/future equipment, and unverified amplifier capacity are not authorized.

decisions: Use three occupied level-0 cores with one requested heavy machine per core.
Reserve at most 500 support heat at the Constructorizer core and at most 350 at each Facturer core.
Reject construction unless every complete per-core heat ledger is at or below 1,000.
Preserve Update 1 authority boundaries and exclude future, hidden, unavailable, or unverified capacity equipment.

Which requested recipes are unlocked, and what measured input rates determine the necessary Update 1 rail tiers?

Complete the per-core heat ledgers before placing machinery.
Build and verify the Constructorizer and two Facturers sequentially at their separate cores.
Commission one recipe lane at a time and validate queues and Fire Wave protection before scaling.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge together with live resumable work state, provenance, checkpoints, and safe next actions so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance work.

The approximately 2,932-token workspace result represents cumulative estimated replay/context across the stateful interaction, not 2,932 tokens of uncached fresh input; cumulative cached replay and uncached input must be reported separately. The frozen one-shot BM25/top-k regression baseline is 17/20 cases, 48/53 evidence items, and approximately 1,070 mean estimated tokens; workspace policy 0.2 also scored 17/20 but recovered 46/53.

The first persistent build slice must open or resume a workspace pinned to immutable revision N, refresh it to N+1 with an explicit evidence/constraint diff, provide batched typed query/read using exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic lane, and commit an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and exact source references. The process-per-operation BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.

The transition passes only when a revision-N parent can consume the N+1 delta in no more than four completed workspace calls, reproduce every direct-filesystem answer claim, avoid full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, emit an immutable child naming its parent and source lineage, and report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input. The frozen 17/20, 48/53, approximately 1,070-token BM25 result remains the regression comparison.

decisions: Build a persistent workspace service rather than extending the process-per-operation BM25 shell.
Implement revision-pinned resume, refresh diffs, batched typed query/read, exact and lexical retrieval, a pluggable semantic lane, and immutable parent-linked checkpoints.
Do not reconstruct the complete prior corpus when the checkpoint and delta suffice.
Keep full source evidence authoritative; summaries, indexes, embeddings, and context packs are derived aids.

next_actions: Implement persistent workspace open/resume with immutable revision pinning.
Implement a machine-readable N-to-N+1 evidence and constraint diff.
